summary: Iter197 · Independent re-verification of (a) Worker/Labour Master week-off rule and (b) Head Office – Delhi real project. Backend pytest 6/6 PASS (/app/backend/tests/test_iter197_worker_rule_and_ho.py): a freshly created employees.master_category='worker' + a staff employee with 26 Present + 4 Weekly_Off days in 2026-11 produces worker.paid_days=26 (is_worker_master=true, week_off_paid=false) and staff.paid_days=30 (is_worker_master=false, week_off_paid=true) via GET /api/hr2/attendance-plus/summary; xlsx and csv exports carry the SAME reduced Paid Days (26 vs 30). Head Office project present exactly ONCE in GET /api/projects as code=HEAD-OFFICE / name='Head Office – Delhi' / is_head_office=true / billing_type=non_billable; test_pm@erp.com DOES get HEAD-OFFICE added to GET /api/projects (via projects_collection_filter PM branch); store@erp.com (store_incharge) does NOT see HEAD-OFFICE. UI verified live on /app/hr/attendance-summary — WORKER badge rendered with data-testid=summary-worker-tag-<emp_id>, worker row Paid Days visibly matches present-only count (WO excluded). Code review confirms rule is wired to employees.master_category=='worker' + is_worker_row helper in hr_worker_rules.py and consumed consistently by attendance_plus_router._summary_data, my_monthly_attendance, payroll_router._compute_payslip and salary_booking_router._att_stats via is_worker_master + paid_weights(week_off_paid=...). No critical issues.
critical_code_review_comments: hr_worker_rules.worker_key_set() loads up to 100 000 employee rows into memory on every attendance-summary request — fine today, but if the employee master grows this should be cached per-request (or memoised with a short TTL). Same call also runs inside my_monthly_attendance which executes on every self-service page view.

attendance_plus_router._summary_data builds the per-employee key with {id: eid, emp_code: e.get('employee_code'), employee_id: e.get('employee_code')} — the dict reuses employee_code for both emp_code AND employee_id. If an attendance row ever stores only the legacy emp_code (not the master's employee_id), is_worker_row's upper-cased key lookup still works because worker_key_set collects both; but the duplication is misleading and should be split for clarity.

head_office_project.ensure_head_office_project() always $sets `type:'internal'`, `status:'active'`, `billing_type:'non_billable'` on every startup — this will stomp any manual edits an admin makes to the HO project through the Projects master UI (e.g. renaming the site, changing status). Consider only $set-on-insert for immutable fields and leave status/billing_type editable thereafter.

scope.projects_collection_filter PM branch ORs {is_head_office:true} unconditionally for PM/Coordinator — good — but there is no equivalent OR for the global apply_project_scope() used by other collections (attendance_plus already special-cases HEAD-OFFICE in match, but Purchase Requisitions / Expenses rely on allowed_project_ids(user) which does NOT include the HO id for a PM). PM sees HO in the project dropdown but may hit 403 'You don't have access to this project' when they then post a PR/expense against ho-delhi. Please verify this chain end-to-end.

head_office_project uses the id 'ho-delhi' only when inserting new — but if the record already exists with a legacy id, we keep that. OK, but there is no uniqueness index on projects.code (checked indirectly) — a race on first-ever boot could still create two HEAD-OFFICE rows before the find_one guard sees them. Add a unique partial index on `code` where `is_head_office:true`.

paid_weights returns float weights only for half_day; everything else is int. Mixed int/float arithmetic is fine but round(paid_days,1) at the end means staff with 30 WO-paid days surfaces as 30 (int-looking) while worker surfaces as 26 — both correct, but downstream payroll uses `factor = paid_days/total_days` so when paid_days==30 and total_days==30 factor==1.0 (good) and worker paid_days==26 gives factor≈0.867 — expected prorated salary cut. Please confirm salary-structure proration on worker payroll runs matches that expectation in the UI.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (WORKER badge + Head Office project visible via API; store_incharge filtered correctly)

test_credentials: admin@erp.com / Admin@123 (super_admin), test_pm@erp.com / PM@12345 (project_manager), store@erp.com / Store@1234 (store_incharge)
seed_data_creation: Pytest module fixture creates 2 TEST_iter197-* employees (worker + staff) with a unique time-based suffix and 30 attendance rows each for 2026-11, then teardown deletes all. UI verification created+deleted one additional UI_iter197 worker. One manual DBG_iter197 employee from exploratory debugging was also deleted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Worker/Labour Master week-off rule and Head Office – Delhi project are both wired correctly. Backend tests are idempotent (unique suffix per run). If re-running, use TEST_MONTH=2026-11 — the fixture auto-cleans. For deeper regression on the HO cost-center expense flow and PR / Expense posting against ho-delhi for a PM user, add dedicated tests — current pass covers scope VISIBILITY only, not full post-mutation permission chain (see critical code review comment #4).
rca of the issue: N/A — session fix verified. Original bug was that is_worker_master() queried the empty legacy hr_workers collection; current implementation (hr_worker_rules.py) reads employees.master_category=='worker' via worker_key_set() + is_worker_row() helpers, which the HR UI actually writes. Confirmed end-to-end: paid_days excludes WO for worker-master only; staff unaffected; exports consistent; UI badge rendered.
